About User Management

What this section does and what each role is allowed to do.

User Management is where administrators control who can sign in to this dashboard and what they are allowed to do. Everyone signs in with their email address. From here you can update your own profile, change your password, and — as an administrator — invite new admins, edit them, change roles, activate or deactivate accounts, reset passwords and remove users.

How it works

Inviting people
  • Add a user with their email, name, phone and role — no password to set
  • They get an email invitation to set their own password (link valid 72 hours)
  • Until they do, their status shows Pending
  • Use Resend invitation if the email is missed or expires
Managing accounts
  • Search by name, ID or email; sort any column; browse with pagination
  • Change a role or activate/deactivate right from the row
  • Select several users to delete them in bulk
  • See each account's last sign-in at a glance
Passwords
  • Reset another user's password from their Edit panel
  • Changing your own password requires your current one
  • Anyone can self-serve via Forgot password on the sign-in screen
Safeguards
  • The last active administrator can't be demoted, deactivated or deleted
  • You can't delete your own account while signed in
  • Deactivating a user blocks their access immediately
Login Activity Logs
  • Automatically log when admins sign in, including IP and Browser/OS
  • Track real-time active duration on the dashboard via a 60s session heartbeat
  • Finalise duration calculation upon explicit logout or when tab/browser is closed
  • Sort, filter, and page through the logs; restricted to Administrators

Roles

Every account has one of three roles. A role decides which areas of the dashboard a person sees and which actions they can take. They are listed below from most to least access.

Administrator Full access

Complete control of the dashboard and all data.

  • Everything Managers and Assistants can do
  • Manage admin users: invite, edit, assign roles, activate/deactivate and delete
  • System settings: Branding, Preferences, Security and Email Logs
  • Delete records and void invoices
Manager Operations

Runs day-to-day operations and finances, without system administration.

  • Manage bookings, inquiries, events, content and newsletter campaigns
  • Full Finance access: invoices, payments and refunds
  • No User Management or System Settings
  • Cannot delete records or void invoices
Assistant Limited

Day-to-day content and booking support with the most limited access.

  • View and manage bookings, inquiries, events and content
  • No Finance: cannot invoice, record payments or refunds
  • No User Management or System Settings
  • Cannot delete records or void invoices

Only Administrators can open the Manage Users tab, invite people and change roles. Give each person the lowest role that still lets them do their job.

About the Inbox

What this section does and how each part works.

The Inbox collects every message a visitor sends through the website's contact and enquiry forms, so you can read, reply to and organise them by status — Unread, Read, Replied or Archived — without anything slipping through the cracks.

How it works

Read & organise
  • Folders filter the list by status, each with a live count
  • Opening a message marks it Read automatically
  • Archive finished messages to keep the inbox tidy
Find messages
  • Search by sender name, email, subject or message text
  • Sort by newest, oldest or sender name
  • Page through large inboxes 50 at a time
Select & bulk actions
  • Tick individual messages or select a whole page
  • Mark several Read or Archive them together
  • Bulk delete is permanent and administrator-only
Reply
  • Respond by email without leaving this page
  • The sender is notified and the message becomes Replied

Common tasks

  1. Reply to a message — open it (this marks it Read), click Reply, write your response and send. The sender is emailed and the message becomes Replied.
  2. Clear the backlog — open the Unread folder, select the page, then Mark read or Archive in one action.
  3. Find an old enquiry — search by sender, email, subject or text and sort by newest, oldest or name.
  4. Keep it tidy — Archive anything you've handled; delete only when a message is truly unwanted.

Deleting a message is permanent and only available to administrators — Archive instead if you may need it later.

Related: Bookings for enquiries that turn into paid engagements; Contact for the public enquiry form and your listed details; and Newsletter to add interested senders to your mailing list.

About Bookings

The operational heart of the platform — how the booking pipeline, the quote/contract/invoice paperwork, and triage all fit together, for both you and the client.

Bookings manages every artist engagement from first contact to final payment. It has two working tabs — the Pipeline (all live bookings) and Booking Recovery (visitors who started a request but didn't finish). Each enquiry moves through an eight-stage lifecycle — New → Pending → Quoted → Accepted → Confirmed → Completed, with Expired and Cancelled as terminal states. Every status transition is validated and recorded server-side — and a separate, non-pipeline Triage flag (further down this page) lets you soft-decline a bad-fit enquiry without cancelling it.

This page reads two ways. The timeline below walks the whole journey stage by stage, spelling out what the client experiences alongside what you see and do at each point. Skip to “How it works” for a quicker reference once you know the shape of it.

The booking lifecycle — client & admin, step by step

Every enquiry travels down this pipeline. Each stage is colour-coded — the same colours you see on the pills and status badges. Client lines describe what the client sees or can do at that point; →Admin lines describe what you see and the action to take.

Phase 1 · Request & Intake
New

A fresh enquiry has arrived — from the public booking form or logged manually — and hasn't been quoted yet. The card now also carries anything the client added: budget range, alternative/backup dates, a content-suitability note, and how they heard about the business.

Client: has just submitted the form (or been logged after a call/email) and is waiting to hear back. No action needed from them yet.

→Admin: review the card, then Send Quote. Left untouched for 24 hours, the system promotes it to Pending on its own and emails the client an “under review” notice.

Pendingauto

Awaiting a quote. A New enquiry becomes Pending automatically after 24 hours if it isn't actioned; it can also be logged directly as Pending.

Client: if they were auto-promoted from New, they received the “still reviewing” email above; otherwise nothing has changed for them yet.

→Admin: Send Quote. Left unquoted, you get a warning digest 24–48h after it first arrived, and it auto-Expires at the 48h mark — the client is notified their request lapsed.

Phase 2 · Quote & Acceptance
Quoted

A formal PDF quote has been generated and emailed with a secure online-accept link; you're waiting on the client's decision.

Client: receives the quote by email and can review and accept it online at their own pace. They also get a reminder email 24h before it lapses if they haven't responded.

→Admin: no action needed — the client's own click drives the next stage. Follow Up if it goes stale, or Revise & Send Quote to replace it (safe here — nothing has been accepted yet). If it lapses unaccepted it auto-Expires; Reopen Booking to try again.

Accepted

The client accepted the quote and agreed to the terms — this is also the moment the invoice and contract paperwork track begins (see “The paperwork track” below). A payment schedule, an invoice and a draft contract are built automatically the instant a booking reaches Accepted, whichever way it got there.

Client: if they clicked Accept online, the invoice is emailed to them immediately — no waiting on you. If you marked it accepted on their behalf (e.g. a phone confirmation), nothing is emailed yet; the invoice sits as a draft for you to check first.

→Admin: if you accepted it yourself, watch for a second toast a couple of seconds later confirming the draft invoice and draft contract were created (or flagging if either failed). Send Invoice if it's still a draft, and start the contract from the Quote & Contract tab — it can only be built or sent from this stage onward.

Phase 3 · Invoice & Payment
Confirmed

The booking is locked in and now appears on the Calendar as an event.

Client: this can happen without you doing anything — the moment they pay any real amount (even just a deposit) on an Accepted invoice, the booking auto-jumps to Confirmed and they get a “booking confirmed” email. If a contract is still awaiting their signature, they can sign it online at any point.

→Admin: if payment hasn't started, send/chase the invoice and record it when it lands. Watch the Deal View's Overview-tab Next Step callout — it now prioritises a client-signed contract waiting on your countersignature above everything else, since that's the one step where they're waiting on you. An amber “Unsigned Contract” badge marks any Confirmed booking whose contract isn't finalised yet.

Phase 4 · Event & Completion
Completedauto

The event has been delivered and the booking is closed.

Client: receives a completion / thank-you email automatically the moment the system closes the booking out, and may later get a review request.

→Admin: this fires automatically only once both the event date has passed and the invoice is fully Paid — the invoice is force-marked Paid at the same moment, for consistency. If the date passes with money still owing, it stays Confirmed with a “Collect & Close” prompt instead (you'll also get an admin digest about it) — collect payment, then mark it Completed yourself. Either way, finish with Request Review.

Off-ramps · terminal states
Expiredterminal

A quote lapsed without acceptance, or a Pending enquiry went stale, without any admin action.

Client: automatically emailed that their request/quote has lapsed. Nothing further is expected of them.

→Admin: nothing is lost — Reopen Booking restores it to Pending so you can quote afresh.

Cancelledterminal

The booking was called off — by the client, by you, by mutual agreement, or force majeure. Its payment status is set to Cancelled too.

Client: receives a cancellation email that states the refund amount owed (if any), which policy rule produced it, and how many days out from the event this was.

→Admin: one cascade fires automatically — the calendar event is removed, any date hold is released, the invoice is voided, pending payment-schedule instalments are cancelled, and a refund is calculated from the cancellation policy. Record the refund once it's paid out, or Book Again to start a fresh booking for the same client.

The paperwork track — Quote, Contract & Invoice run in parallel

Once a booking reaches Accepted, three linked-but-independent documents move through their own small lifecycles alongside the main pipeline above. They don't have their own pills on the board — you track them from the Quote & Contract and Invoices & Payments tabs inside the booking.

Quote
  • draft → sent → accepted, or archived/void the moment a newer version replaces it
  • Re-quoting an Accepted/Confirmed booking is a live change to a committed deal, not a fresh draft — see the warning below
  • If the client sits on an emailed quote too long, they get an automatic follow-up nudge; you get a separate alert if an Accepted booking still has no invoice after a few days
Contract
  • draft → sent → signed — only buildable/sendable once the booking is Accepted or later
  • Client signs online first; you countersign to finalise — countersigning is normally blocked until the client has signed
  • Countersigning re-checks the signed PDF's fingerprint and shows a “Document integrity verified” note (or a red alert if it doesn't match — effectively a tamper check)
  • A signed & finalised contract can no longer be built, edited or re-sent
Invoice
  • DRAFT → SENT → OVERDUE → PAID, or VOID
  • Generate Invoice always creates a silent draft for you to check first — the client is only emailed once you click Send. The one exception: a client accepting their own quote online is emailed the invoice immediately, no draft step
  • A sent, unpaid invoice past its due date is automatically flagged Overdue overnight; going Void requires a reason and is admin-only

Re-quoting an Accepted/Confirmed booking automatically resets its contract to Draft — even a signed one. The signature is cleared and a fresh send-and-sign is required at the new figure, and the live invoice plus any pending payment instalments are voided/superseded at the same time. If you initiate the re-quote yourself you'll see a confirmation naming this before it happens; if a client's own action triggers it, the amber drift warning on the Quote & Contract tab is how you'll notice afterwards.

Payment status

Tracked separately from the booking status above — a Completed booking can still be Unpaid, so always check both.

Paid Deposit Paid Partially Paid Unpaid Payment Failed

A client's own payment can move the booking forward with zero action from you. The instant they pay anything real (even a partial deposit) through the invoice's payment link on an Accepted or Confirmed booking, it auto-jumps straight to Confirmed. Paying in full on an earlier-stage booking jumps it to Accepted. Check the Overview tab's next-step hint after any payment lands — it may already have moved.

Booking Triage — soft-declining without cancelling

Every booking also carries a disposition — Active (the default), Not a Fit, or Archived — a completely separate flag from the status pipeline above. It exists for enquiries that were never really going anywhere: wrong budget, wrong content, spam, a duplicate. Cancelling one of those would count it as a deal that fell through and skew your conversion numbers; Triage lets you set it aside cleanly instead.

Client side
  • The client never sees or is told about this — it is purely an internal note for you
  • It doesn't touch their booking's status, and no email is triggered by a disposition change
Admin side
  • Open the row's More menu → Mark Not a Fit or Archive; Restore to Active reverses it at any time
  • The Bookings list's disposition filter defaults to Active, hiding triaged rows — switch it to Not a Fit / Archived / All to find them again
  • A grey badge marks a triaged booking wherever it appears, and it's excluded from the pipeline's pending/quoted/confirmed counts

How it works

The lifecycle
  • Eight stages carry a booking from enquiry to completion; each stage colour-coded
  • Status only advances through validated actions inside a card — never by editing a field, and several steps also advance automatically (see the timeline's “auto” tags above)
  • You can't skip stages or move backwards past a terminal state — disposition (Active/Not a Fit/Archived) is the separate, non-pipeline way to set an enquiry aside
Pills & filters
  • The coloured pills are filter shortcuts, not status changers — each shows a live count
  • One dropdown filters by booking status or payment status; a second filters by disposition (defaults to Active) — all three are independent
  • Search by name, email, event or booking ID; Clear filters resets every filter, including disposition, back to its default
Inside a booking
  • Click any card to open the Deal View — six tabs: Overview (summary + next-step hint), Quote & Contract, Invoices & Payments, Advancing (event-day logistics), Timeline & Notes, and Files
  • The Overview tab's callout always names the single next action — and now weighs a client-signed contract awaiting your countersignature above a payment chase
  • An amber “Unsigned Contract” badge flags any Accepted/Confirmed/Completed booking whose contract isn't finalised yet; confirming or completing one still works, but warns you first
  • Every action is timestamped to the audit trail in Security
Create & sync
  • New enquiry opens the manual booking modal for phone / email leads
  • Refresh reloads the pipeline and re-syncs the Calendar
  • Deleting a booking is administrator-only and permanent
Booking Recovery
  • Lists visitors who started a request but didn't submit; the tab badge shows how many
  • Resend a reminder to anyone manually at any time
  • Automatic reminders go only to those who reached the final step and consented — up to 3 nudges (roughly 1h, then +24h, then +72h later), and an unconverted draft is purged after 30 days

Common tasks

  1. Log a phone / email lead — click New enquiry, fill in the client and event details, and save. It enters the pipeline as New.
  2. Move a booking forward — open the card, send a quote, mark it accepted, confirm the date, then mark it completed once the job is done.
  3. Get a contract signed — on an Accepted booking, open Quote & Contract, Build the contract, Send it to the client, then Countersign once they've signed online to finalise it.
  4. Soft-decline a bad-fit enquiry — instead of cancelling it, open the row's More menu and choose Mark Not a Fit or Archive; it drops out of the pipeline view without counting as a lost deal.
  5. Change the terms after acceptance — re-quoting an Accepted/Confirmed booking is allowed, but read the confirmation carefully: it resets any existing contract to Draft (clearing a signature if there was one) and voids the live invoice.
  6. Find what needs chasing — set the dropdown to a booking status (e.g. Confirmed) or a payment status (e.g. Unpaid) to isolate exactly those cards; remember the disposition filter is separate and defaults to hiding triaged rows.
  7. Recover a lost request — open the Booking Recovery tab and use Resend to nudge an abandoned enquiry.

Booking status and payment status are separate. A Completed booking can still be Unpaid — always check both before you consider an engagement closed.

All status transitions, quotes, contracts, invoices and payments are validated and recorded server-side with an audit trail — the pipeline view is a window onto that, not the source of truth. Deleting a booking is permanent and cannot be undone; a signed & finalised contract cannot be edited or replaced either — only a re-quote can supersede it.

You'll get a digest email, not just an in-app badge, for the things worth chasing: PENDING enquiries about to auto-expire, an Accepted booking that still has no invoice after a few days, and CONFIRMED bookings whose event date has passed with payment still outstanding. Treat those as prompts to open the booking, not just the badges on the board.

About Calendar

How the unified calendar works and what each control does.

The Calendar is the command centre for every date-sensitive item — bookings, date holds, public events, and financial milestones. It renders a full interactive calendar with colour-coded entries and a three-panel sidebar for quick navigation, schedule management, and an upcoming-events snapshot.

How it works

Colour filters
  • The filter bar toggles visibility for Bookings, Holds, Events, and Milestones
  • Each category has its own colour — see the legend below the calendar for the full key
  • Click any calendar event to view or edit its details
Date holds & blocks
  • Block Out Dates creates a hold that prevents public bookings on those days
  • Holds can span multiple days and be categorised (Travel, Unavailable, etc.)
  • Click a day in the mini-calendar sidebar to quickly create a hold
Working hours & schedule
  • The Schedule sidebar tab configures working hours per day of the week
  • The booking gap setting adds buffer time between events on the public form
  • Non-working days are automatically marked unavailable on the public booking calendar
iCalendar feed
  • Copy Feed URL copies the .ics subscription link for Google Calendar, Outlook, or Apple Calendar
  • The feed updates automatically as bookings and holds change
  • External calendar apps may take up to 24 hours to refresh the feed

Common tasks

  1. Block out dates — drag to select a range on the calendar (or click a day in the mini-calendar), set the range and a category, and save. Those days become unavailable on the public booking form.
  2. Set your working hours — open the Schedule sidebar tab, set hours per day of the week and the booking-gap buffer.
  3. Subscribe elsewhere — use Copy Feed URL and paste the link into Google, Outlook or Apple Calendar.
  4. Review an entry — click any colour-coded event to view or edit its details.

All calendar entries are validated server-side. Date holds enforce availability rules on the public booking form, and booking events are kept in sync with the Pipeline in real time.

Related: Bookings, whose confirmed engagements appear here automatically; Finance, whose payment milestones show as entries; and Events for public event dates.

About Finance

The financial ledger — revenue, invoices, expenses, reconciliation and payment reminders for your bookings.

The Financial Ledger tracks every rand in and out of the business. The tiles at the top reflect the selected period, where Net Profit = Revenue − Expenses. The Overdue and Due Soon tiles are clickable shortcuts that jump straight to the matching invoices.

How it works

Tiles & period
  • Pick the period first — every tile and total respects it
  • Overdue and Due Soon tiles jump to the matching invoices
Transactions & Invoices
  • Every payment received and every invoice raised, with filters
  • Invoices are raised from a booking in the Pipeline
  • Voiding an invoice is administrator-only
Expenses
  • Costs are manually logged via Log Expense
  • Logged expenses feed directly into Net Profit
Reconciliation
  • Compares quoted amounts against PayFast and manual payments
  • Flags discrepancies so nothing is under- or over-collected
Reminders
  • Automated payment reminders for outstanding invoices
  • Timing is configured in Legal & Compliance → Booking Policies
Analytics & Reports
  • Revenue trend, debt ageing and top clients at a glance

Common tasks

  1. Chase an overdue invoice — click the Overdue tile to jump to those invoices, then send a reminder.
  2. Log an expense — open the Expenses tab, click Log Expense; it lowers Net Profit for the period.
  3. Check the books balance — open Reconciliation to spot any gap between quotes and payments received.
  4. Change reminder timing — head to Legal & Compliance → Booking Policies.

Always set the period before reading the tiles — a “low revenue” month is often just a narrow date range.

Finance is available to Managers and Administrators only — Assistants can't see it. Voiding invoices and deleting records is administrator-only, and financial records are retained for the legally required 5-year SARS period even after a POPIA erasure.

Related: Bookings, where invoices and payments originate; Legal & Compliance for reminder and policy settings; and Security for the financial audit trail and POPIA erasure.

About Services

The priced catalogue items used when building quotes and invoices for bookings.

The Services Catalogue holds reusable, priced items — performances, travel, production lines and more. When you build a quote for a booking, you pick from the active services listed here, so pricing stays consistent across every engagement.

How it works

What a service is
  • A reusable catalogue item — a performance, travel, a production line, etc.
  • Quotes are assembled by picking from the active services here
Pricing models
  • Flat Fee — one fixed price
  • Per Minute / Per Hour — price × quantity, with min/max limits
Active vs Inactive
  • Inactive services are hidden from new quotes
  • Making a service inactive doesn't change existing bookings
Advanced fields
  • GL codes, crew, tax class and more for accounting integration
  • All optional — a name, price and model are enough to start
Archive vs Delete
  • Archiving is reversible — the item just leaves new quotes
  • A service used by existing booking line items can't be hard-deleted

Common tasks

  1. Add a service — click Add Service, set the name, category, pricing model and price, then save. It's active by default.
  2. Retire a service — set it Inactive to hide it from new quotes, or Archive it to remove it reversibly.
  3. Reprice — edit the price; quotes that already used the old price are left untouched.

Keep the catalogue lean — mark seasonal or one-off items Inactive rather than deleting them, so their history stays intact.

Changing a service's price does not retroactively change quotes that already used it — you'll be warned if active drafts reference it.

Related: Bookings, where these services become quote line items; and Finance, where those quotes turn into invoices and revenue.

Booking Policies

About the Legal & Consent Centre

Draft, version and publish your public legal documents — and keep the consent trail that proves compliance.

This centre manages everything legal and compliance-related for your public site: the Privacy Policy, Terms of Use and Cookie & Consent wording your visitors see, plus the records that prove you're compliant — the Consent Audit, the Contract Registry and full Version History. Booking Policies sets the rules that Bookings and Finance enforce.

How it works

Legal documents
  • Edit Privacy Policy, Terms of Use and Cookie & Consent wording in a rich-text editor
  • Save as Draft while you work, Publish Now to go live
Versioning & history
  • Every publish creates a version stamped with your change summary
  • Version History shows the full trail across all documents
  • A published version can't be rewritten — only superseded
Consent Audit
  • Records who consented, when, from which IP and to which policy version
  • Search and export to CSV for your records
  • Read-only evidence — entries aren't edited by hand
Contract Registry
  • Tracks signed and draft contracts in one place
  • Counts surface on the Overview tiles at a glance
Booking Policies
  • Deposit terms, cancellation rules and payment-reminder timing
  • These rules are enforced over in Bookings and Finance

Common tasks

  1. Update a policy — open Privacy Policy, Terms of Use or Cookie & Consent, edit, write a change summary, Save as Draft, then Publish Now.
  2. Prove consent — open Consent Audit, search by name, email or IP, and Export CSV.
  3. Review what changed — open Version History to see every published version and its note.
  4. Adjust booking rules — open Booking Policies to change deposit and cancellation terms or reminder timing.

Always write a clear change summary before publishing — it becomes the permanent version note, so future-you can see exactly what changed and when.

Publish Now updates the live public site on the next page load — draft first. Consent and contract records are legal evidence: treat them as read-only and export via CSV rather than altering them. Legal edits are administrator-only.

Common tasks

  2. Embed a video or post — on the Media Embeds tab, click Add Media Embed and paste the link or embed code.
  3. Configure Dashboard KPIs — on the Dashboard KPIs tab, select your preferred data source for each platform. If "Manual Input" is chosen, specify your follower counts and trend rates, then click Save KPI Settings.
  4. Hide something temporarily — set the item Inactive instead of deleting it, so you can bring it back later.

Understanding Dashboard KPIs

The Dashboard KPIs tab feeds the five follower cards in the Social Media Channels grid at the top of the main dashboard, giving you your aggregate digital footprint in one view. Configure each platform independently, then click Save KPI Settings — the dashboard updates immediately. Here's what each field controls:

Data Source
  • Live API — pulls the real count from the platform automatically (cached up to 1 hour).
  • Manual — you type the numbers in yourself; no API needed.
Follower Count

Your current audience size on that platform (e.g. 12345). The dashboard formats it with commas — 12,345.

Goal / TargetNew

The milestone you're aiming for. It sets how full the progress bar under each card looks — e.g. 15,080 of a 25,000 goal fills the bar to 60%.

Trend %

The growth rate over a recent interval, entered as a positive number (e.g. 5.5). The sign comes from Direction, so you never type a minus.

Trend Direction
  • Up (+) — green badge, upward arrow, shown as +5.5%.
  • Down (−) — red badge, downward arrow, shown as −5.5%.

Getting your Live API credentials

To switch a platform to Live API, paste credentials from that platform's developer console into its card on the Dashboard KPIs tab, then click Save KPI Settings. These are stored on the server (admin-only) and the dashboard refreshes them hourly. New to this? Start with YouTube — it's the quickest and needs no approval.

YouTube Easiest

Needs: API Key + Channel ID

  • In Google Cloud Console, create a project.
  • Enable YouTube Data API v3 (APIs & Services → Library).
  • Create an API key under Credentials.
  • Copy the Channel ID (channel page → Share → Copy channel ID, starts with UC…).
Facebook

Needs: Page Access Token + Page ID

  • You must be an admin of the Facebook Page (not a personal profile).
  • Create a Business app at Meta for Developers.
  • In the Graph API Explorer: Get Token → Get Page Access Token, allow pages_read_engagement.
  • Run me/accounts to list each Page's id (the Page ID) and token.
Instagram

Needs: Access Token + User ID

  • Uses the same Meta app as Facebook.
  • Requires an IG Business / Creator account linked to a Facebook Page.
  • Get the IG User ID via {page-id}?fields=instagram_business_account.
  • Token needs instagram_basic + pages_read_engagement.
X (Twitter)

Needs: Bearer Token + Username

  • Create a project/app in the X Developer Portal.
  • Copy the app's Bearer Token from Keys & Tokens.
  • Enter your handle without the @.
  • The free tier is heavily rate-limited.
TikTok

Needs: Access Token

  • Register an app at TikTok for Developers.
  • Add Login Kit and request the user.info.stats scope.
  • Complete OAuth to obtain a user Access Token.

Watch token expiry. Facebook, Instagram, X and TikTok tokens from the quick-start tools are usually short-lived (~1 hour), so a card can stop updating soon after you save. For a lasting connection, exchange them for a long-lived / non-expiring token — for Facebook, a Page token via the token-exchange endpoint. YouTube API keys don't expire. If a fetch fails, the dashboard keeps the last saved number instead of breaking.

Troubleshooting

A card shows old numbers

Live values are cached for up to an hour. Save the platform again to refresh sooner, or switch it to Manual for an instant change.

A live card stopped updating

The access token has most likely expired. Generate a long-lived / non-expiring token and paste it into the platform's card again.

The count looks wrong

Check the Channel / Page / User ID matches the right account — a mismatched ID returns someone else's figures, or none at all.

X (Twitter) won't update

The free API tier is heavily rate-limited and often returns nothing. Wait and try later, or keep X on Manual.

Trend arrow is the wrong colour

The sign and colour follow the Direction field, not the number you type. Set Up or Down explicitly to fix it.

Progress bar looks off

The bar is relative to the Goal / Target. Set a realistic goal so the fill reflects real progress.

Data & permissions

Where your data is stored
  • Live-API credentials (keys & tokens) — on the server, admin-only, used for the hourly refresh.
  • KPI values & goals — on the server, in the analytics database.
  • Social links & media embeds — on the server.
  • The Media Embeds API-key field is the exception — it stays in this browser (local storage).
Who can manage this
  • All admin roles can view everything and add or edit links & embeds.
  • Administrators & Managers can save Dashboard KPI settings.
  • Only Administrators can delete a social link or media embed.

Mix and match. Each platform's data source is independent — run YouTube live while the rest stay manual, in any combination.

Safety net. If a live fetch fails, the dashboard keeps the last saved number, so cards never go blank.

Use Active / Inactive to curate what visitors see without losing anything — retired links and embeds stay saved and ready to re-enable.

Your Media Embeds API-key field is saved in this browser (local storage), not on the server — avoid entering it on a shared or public computer. Dashboard-KPI credentials are different: those are stored securely on the server.

          About System Settings

          Gateway, mail-server and notification settings that power online payments and every system email.

          The Settings tab is organised into three cards — PayFast, Email (SMTP) and Notifications. Everything saves together with the single Save System Settings button and takes effect immediately — no restart. Leaving a field blank keeps its current saved value. Below is what every field does and how to fill it in.

          How it works

          PayFast

          Connects the public booking flow to the PayFast gateway so clients can pay deposits and invoices online. If these are wrong or empty, online card payments won't go through.

          • Merchant ID & Merchant Key — your PayFast account credentials (PayFast dashboard → Settings → Integration).
          • Passphrase — an optional security salt that signs each transaction. It is never shown back for safety — the field stays blank with a “set” hint; leave it blank to keep the current one, or type a new value to replace it.
          • Gateway URL — use the sandbox URL (sandbox.payfast.co.za) while testing, and switch to the live URL (www.payfast.co.za) when you go live.

          Always test in sandbox first — a mismatched key or passphrase makes payments fail PayFast's signature check.

          Email (SMTP)

          The outgoing mail server used for every system email — quotes, booking confirmations, payment receipts, password resets and the new user invitation emails. If email stops working, this is the first place to check.

          • SMTP Host — your mail provider's server, e.g. smtp.gmail.com.
          • Port — 587 for STARTTLS (most common) or 465 for SSL.
          • From Address — the address recipients see the email coming from.
          • SMTP User & Password — the mailbox login. For Gmail / Google Workspace, turn on 2-step verification and use an App Password, not your normal password.

          Notifications

          Where the system's internal alerts are delivered.

          • Notifications Email — the inbox that receives new-booking alerts, overdue-payment warnings and other admin notices.
          • Send Test — emails a sample message to that address right now, so you can confirm your SMTP settings actually work. Use it whenever you change the Email (SMTP) card.

          Common tasks

          1. Connect PayFast — paste your Merchant ID, Merchant Key and (optionally) passphrase, set the sandbox URL to test, then switch to the live URL and Save System Settings.
          2. Set up email — enter the SMTP host, port, from-address and login, save, then use Send Test to confirm mail actually delivers.
          3. Route admin alerts — set the Notifications Email so new-booking and overdue-payment notices reach the right inbox.

          After changing the Email (SMTP) card, always click Send Test — a silent mis-configuration here stops quotes, receipts and password resets from ever arriving.

          • All three cards are saved together by the single Save System Settings button, and changes apply immediately — no server restart.
          • Leaving a field blank keeps its current saved value; it won't be wiped.
          • Only Administrators can open System Settings.

          Related: Finance, where PayFast payments are recorded; Newsletter and User Management, which rely on the SMTP server to send mail; and Email Logs to confirm what actually went out.

          Master Banner System

          About the Master Banner System

          How per-category banner images get attached to your outgoing emails.

          Every client-facing email belongs to one of 12 fixed categories (Booking Requests, Quotes & Proposals, Contracts & Signatures, Payments & Invoices, Booking Confirmations, Event Reminders, Thank You & Reviews, Booking Recovery, Contact & Support, Newsletters & Marketing, User Accounts & Security, Birthday). A banner is one image assigned to a category and, from there, to any number of specific email templates via the Assign action on its card.

          Banners are resolved at the moment an email sends — there is no publish step. Editing a banner's image, headline or subtitle updates every template using it immediately. If a template has no banner assigned, or its banner is archived, the email falls back to a plain text headline block instead — nothing breaks, it just looks less photographic.

          Image specs

          • JPG or PNG only
          • 1200–1400px wide (2× retina; displays at 600–700px)
          • 100KB or smaller
          • Descriptive alt text is required — it's what shows if the image is blocked, and it matters for accessibility and deliverability

          A few things to know

          • Personalisation (names, booking references, amounts) always lives in the email text, never baked into the banner image itself
          • Buttons are never part of the artwork — every call-to-action is a real, clickable button below the banner
          • Emails render in dark mode by default; banner art should hold up on a near-black background
          • Only PREMIUM (client/visitor/subscriber-facing) emails use banners — internal SYSTEM notifications (digests, alerts, password resets) use a compact text header instead

          Use the Preview tab to see exactly how any template looks with its currently assigned banner (or its fallback) before you rely on it.

          Admin Login Background

          Full-screen image shown behind the admin sign-in screen. A landscape photo around 1920×1080 works best.

          Click Save Site Settings to apply. Restore default clears it back to the sign-in screen's built-in background.

          Changes apply to the admin sign-in screen after saving.

          About Branding

          Your logo, favicon, accent colour, fonts and imagery — the visual identity applied across the public site, the dashboard and every email.

          Branding is grouped into a few sets of settings. Upload an image (or paste a URL) and a preview appears straight away — then click that tab's Save button (Save Identity or Save Site Settings) to apply. Saved values live on the server, so they're identical on every device and take effect immediately.

          How it works

          Identity

          • Header / Site Logo — shown in the website header, replacing the text wordmark. (Emails use the separate Email Banner below.)
          • Favicon — the small icon in browser tabs (16×16 or 32×32 px).
          • Primary Accent Colour — the gold/highlight colour used for buttons and accents across the site and dashboard.
          • Theme Font — the typeface used site-wide.

          Email Banners

          • Banner Library (under the Banners tab) manages a per-category banner image system — one image can be assigned to any number of email templates (quotes, confirmations, invoices, and more), and updates every email using it the moment you save.
          • See the Banners tab's own About view for the full picture: categories, image specs, and how assignment works.

          Site

          • Admin Login Background — the full-screen image behind the admin sign-in screen. It is saved on the server, so everyone who opens the login page sees it; it is automatically hidden once you're inside the dashboard.
          • Click Restore default (or clear the URL field) and Save Site Settings — the sign-in screen returns to its default background.

          Common tasks

          1. Swap the logo — under Identity, upload the header logo (or paste a URL), check the preview, and Save Identity.
          2. Set the accent colour — under Identity, pick the primary accent colour used for buttons and highlights, then save.
          3. Brand your emails — under Banners, create a banner and assign it to one or more email templates.
          4. Change the login screen — under Site, set the Admin Login Background (clear the field to reset it), then save.

          A preview appears the moment you upload, but nothing reaches visitors until you click that tab's Save button — don't navigate away expecting an un-saved preview to stick.

          • Uploads show a live preview here in the panel; the change goes live only after that tab's Save button.
          • Branding applies to the public website and the admin dashboard; only the Login Background is admin-only.
          • Only Administrators can change branding.

          Related: About Me and Home Slider for the public content this styles; Newsletter, which wraps campaigns in this brand; and System Settings for the mail server behind branded emails.

          About Email Logs

          A read-only record of every email the system sends.

          Every outgoing system email is logged here automatically. This view is read-only — entries cannot be edited or deleted. Use the search box, the status / event filters, and the sortable columns to trace any message.

          What gets logged

          • New booking notifications
          • Formal quotes sent to clients
          • Payment-received confirmations
          • Contact-form inquiry alerts
          • Newsletter campaign dispatches
          • Admin direct messages
          • Password-reset requests

          Delivery statuses

          • Success — accepted by the mail server
          • Failed — could not be delivered
          • Pending — queued, delivery not yet confirmed

          Common tasks

          1. Trace a message — use the search box (recipient or subject) together with the status and event filters, then sort by date.
          2. Investigate a failure — filter by Failed to see what didn't deliver, then check System Settings → Email (SMTP).
          3. Confirm a send — filter by event type (e.g. a quote or password reset) and read the status column.

          This log is read-only and can't be edited or cleared — treat it as the definitive delivery audit trail when a client says an email never arrived.

          Related: System Settings for the SMTP server that sends these emails; Newsletter, Bookings and Finance, which trigger most of them; and Security for the wider change audit trail.

          About Security & Audit

          System health, the change audit trail and POPIA data erasure — the tools that keep the platform secure and compliant.

          Security & Audit is where administrators watch the platform's health, review an immutable record of every change, and honour data-privacy requests. Everything in this section is administrator-only.

          How it works

          System Integrity
          • Live health snapshot — database sync, SSL/TLS encryption, session-expiry monitoring
          • Lists recent administrator sign-ins at a glance
          Audit Trail
          • Records every change to bookings, invoices, transactions, cancellations and quotations — who, what and when
          • Search and filter by table, action, user or date range
          • Entries are immutable — they can't be edited or deleted
          POPIA Data Erasure
          • Anonymises a client's personal identifiers on request
          • Financial records are kept for the legally required 5-year SARS period; only personal data is replaced
          • Irreversible — the original personal data cannot be recovered

          Common tasks

          1. Check the platform's health — open System Integrity to confirm sync, encryption and session status, and see who signed in recently.
          2. Trace a change — on the Audit Trail, search by table, action or user and set a date range to find exactly what happened.
          3. Honour an erasure request — use POPIA Data Erasure to anonymise a client (financial totals stay intact).

          The Audit Trail is your accountability record — check it first whenever a figure, status or booking looks wrong, before assuming a bug.

          POPIA erasure is permanent and can't be undone, and the audit trail can't be edited or deleted. This entire section is administrator-only — grant that role sparingly.

          Related: User Management for roles and login-activity logs; Finance, whose records the 5-year retention protects; and Email Logs for outbound-mail history.

          Privacy Policy

          Last Updated: 31 March 2026
          1. Introduction

          Welcome to the official website of Thabiso Mhlongo. We respect your privacy and are committed to protecting the personal information you share with us.

          2. Information We Collect
          • Contact & booking forms: Name, email, phone, event details, and notes.
          • Newsletter subscriptions: Your email address.
          • Technical/usage data: IP address, browser type, and pages visited via server logs.

          We do not collect payment card details — payments are processed securely by PayFast.

          3. How We Use Your Information
          • To respond to contact and booking requests.
          • To send newsletters to opted-in subscribers.
          • To generate booking quotes and email correspondence.
          • To improve website performance and security.
          • To comply with applicable legal obligations.
          4. Cookies & Local Storage
          • Session cookies: Admin authentication sessions only.
          • Local storage: Cookie consent preference and personalisation settings.
          • Third-party embeds: YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, Facebook may set their own cookies.
          5. Your Rights (POPIA)

          Under South Africa’s POPIA, you have the right to access, correct, or delete your data, and to unsubscribe from newsletters at any time. Contact: bookings@thabisomhlongo.com

          6. Data Security

          We implement bcrypt password hashing, session-based authentication, rate limiting on public forms, and duplicate submission prevention.

          7. Changes to This Policy

          We may update this policy at any time. Continued use of the website after changes constitutes acceptance of the revised policy.

          Thabiso Mhlongo — bookings@thabisomhlongo.com
